mainTopic: Finishing פדיון הבן (שטר, returning the money, lost money, death after thirty days) and the בכור's double share
overview: This amud finishes the laws of פדיון הבן and then begins the laws of the בכור's inheritance. First, the גמרא explains the משנה about a father who writes the כהן a debt note. עולא says that by Torah law the son is redeemed, but the רבנן made a גזירה so people would not think you can redeem with a שטר. רב נחמן shows that a ברייתא saying otherwise is a minority view, and the הלכה is that the son is not redeemed. Next, the כהן may give the money back as a gift. רבי טרפון did this and was praised, but רבי חנינא ruled that a father who gave the money expecting it back did not redeem his son. For money that was set aside and lost, ריש לקיש and רבי יונתן offer גזירות שוות, but רב פפא says the source is the משנה's own verse. He moves their teachings to the case of a son who died after thirty days, where the father, or his heirs, must still pay. Finally, a new משנה teaches that the בכור takes a double share only of his father's property, and only of what the father actually held.

steps.title: Consecrated items are not redeemed with these things either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its re-reading of the משנה: הקדשות, like a בכור, cannot be redeemed with slaves, documents, or land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And consecrated items are not redeemed with any of these.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a discussion from the previous section. The גמרא gives its final reading of the משנה's words "ולא בהקדשות".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the משנה seems to say you cannot redeem a בכור using הקדש items. The גמרא reads it differently: הקדשות themselves cannot be redeemed with slaves, שטרות, or land. This puts הקדש in the same group as פדיון הבן for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated items that belong to the Temple
With any of these (slaves, documents, land)

phrases.english: And consecrated items are not redeemed with any of these.
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא is reading the משנה's words "ולא בהקדשות" in a new way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the re-reading of the משנה that began earlier.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Slaves, documents, and land cannot be used to redeem a בכור, and they cannot be used to redeem הקדש either.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about writing a debt note to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a father who writes the כהן a note for five סלעים must pay, but his son is not redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote to the כהן that he owes him five סלעים, he must give them to him, etc. (and his son is not redeemed).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father has bound himself to pay through a written note. The משנה says the debt is real and he must pay. Still, his son is not redeemed by the note. The question will be why the son is not redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: Sela coins; five are needed for פדיון הבן

phrases.english: If he wrote to a kohen that he owes him
phrases.notes: The father writes a note of debt.

phrases.english: five sela'im,
he is obligated to give to him, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה line: "and his son is not redeemed."

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתַב לְכֹהֵן שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב לוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה סְלָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Writing a debt note obligates the father to pay, but it does not redeem the son.

steps.title: עולא: By Torah law the son is redeemed
steps.stepSummary: עולא says that by Torah law the son is actually redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: By Torah law, his son is redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא makes a surprising statement. He says that according to the Torah itself, the son is redeemed in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the son is not redeemed. עולא says this is not a Torah rule. Since the father truly owes the כהן five סלעים, the Torah would count the son as redeemed. This creates a gap that the next step must explain.
steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not disagreeing with the משנה. He accepts that in practice the son is not redeemed. He only explains that this rule comes from the רבנן, not from the Torah.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
By Torah law, his son is redeemed;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what kind of rule the משנה's ruling is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under Torah law, the son is redeemed when the father has bound himself to pay.

steps.title: Then why is the son not redeemed?
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah counts the son as redeemed, why does the משנה say he is not?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that his son is not redeemed?
steps.whatsHappening: Right after his statement, עולא asks the obvious question. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says the son is redeemed, but the משנה says he is not. Something must explain the difference. The question asks for that reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason his son is not redeemed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question that comes directly from the gap עולא just created.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה says the son is not redeemed, if the Torah counts him as redeemed.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree so people won't think you can redeem with a document
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן made a גזירה: otherwise people might think you can redeem a בכור with a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, lest people say that one may redeem with a document.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers his own question. The son is not redeemed because of a rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the son counted as redeemed here, people might think a document itself can be used to redeem. The משנה already ruled that you cannot redeem with שטרות. So the רבנן cancelled the redemption in this case, to protect that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: One may redeem with a document

steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law the son is redeemed. Only a גזירה of the רבנן, made to protect the rule that you cannot redeem with שטרות, makes the משנה say he is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a case that works under Torah law is blocked by the רבנן because it looks like a forbidden case.

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest they say
that one may redeem with a document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling is a rabbinic גזירה, so that people will not think a שטר can be used for redemption.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the son is redeemed once the father pays
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רב נחמן: the son is redeemed once the father actually pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב נחמן: His son is redeemed when he gives.
steps.whatsHappening: A new source is brought. A ברייתא seems to disagree with the משנה, because it says the son becomes redeemed once the money is paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the son is not redeemed through the note. This ברייתא says that once the father actually pays the debt, the redemption takes effect. That seems to clash with the משנה's ruling.

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav Nachman:
His son is redeemed when he gives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that seems to conflict with the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the father pays, the son is redeemed.

steps.title: רב נחמן: That ברייתא is a minority opinion
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the ברייתא follows a single sage, but the חכמים say the son is not redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: This is the statement of רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה, recorded without a name. Some say: This is the statement of רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון, recorded without a name. But the חכמים say: His son is not redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן takes away the ברייתא's force. He says it is the opinion of one sage, written without his name, and the majority disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of who wrote the ברייתא: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה or רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Either way it is one sage, and the חכמים hold that the son is not redeemed. So the ברייתא does not override the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Recorded anonymously, without the author's name

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: This is the statement of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda
recorded without attribution;
phrases.notes: This is just a spelling fix: some versions have the word in round brackets, and the square brackets show the corrected spelling.

phrases.english: and some say: This is the statement of
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, recorded without attribution;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי.
phrases.english: but the Sages say: His son is not redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא from Step 6 by showing it is a minority view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ברייתא is not rejected as false. It is limited to one sage's opinion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא represents one sage only, and the majority חכמים disagree.

steps.title: The הלכה: the son is not redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like the חכמים: the son is not redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: His son is not redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling. This settles the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows the חכמים and the משנה, not the ברייתא. A debt note does not redeem the son, even after the father pays it.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is that the son is not redeemed through a note of debt. This fits עולא's explanation of the גזירה.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: His son is not redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the disagreement from Steps 6 and 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The son is not redeemed through a שטר of debt.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the כהן may return the money as a gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the כהן may give the five סלעים back to the father as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, if the כהן wishes to give it to him as a gift, he is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up the comment that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the money really belongs to the כהן, he may do whatever he wants with it, even give it back to the father. The word לפיכך links this rule to what the משנה said before it.

phrases.english: Therefore, if the kohen wishes
to give it to him as a gift, he is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ אִם רָצָה הַכֹּהֵן לִיתֵּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן may give the redemption money back to the father as a gift.

steps.title: The משנה already teaches a ברייתא's rulings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה already teaches a ברייתא: giving to ten כהנים at once or one after another works, and so does a כהן taking the money and returning it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have already learned what the רבנן taught: If he gave it to ten כהנים at once, he fulfilled his duty. One after the other, he fulfilled it. If the כהן took it and returned it to him, he fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that our משנה already contains the ruling of a known ברייתא. It then quotes the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows the כהן to return the money as a gift. That is the same as the ברייתא's last case: "took it and returned it, he fulfilled it." The ברייתא also adds that the father may give the money to ten כהנים together, or to several כהנים one after another.
steps.confusionAlert: Returning the money does not cancel the redemption. The father truly gave it, the כהן truly owned it, and then the כהן chose to give it back.
steps.whatToRemember: The redemption works once a כהן truly receives the five סלעים. It works even if the money is split among many כהנים, or if the כהן gives it back as a gift.

phrases.english: We have learned in the Mishnah that which the Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: נְתָנוֹ לַעֲשָׂרָה כֹּהֲנִים בְּבַת אַחַת — יָצָא,
phrases.english: If he gave it to ten kohanim at once, he fulfilled his duty;
one after the other, he fulfilled his duty;
if the kohen took it and returned it to him, he fulfilled his duty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the משנה just quoted already teaches a ברייתא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's rule that a כהן who took the money and returned it still leaves the father's duty fulfilled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's statement that the כהן may give the money back as a gift.

steps.title: רבי טרפון would take the money and give it back
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on: רבי טרפון used to take the redemption money and return it, and the חכמים praised him, saying he kept this הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this was the habit of רבי טרפון: he would take the money and give it back. When the חכמים heard about it, they said: 'This man kept this הלכה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step continues with a real-life example. רבי טרפון actually did what the הלכה allows: he took the five סלעים and then gave them back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said a כהן may take the money and return it. Now we see a great sage doing this in practice, and the חכמים approving it. This shows that taking and returning is not a trick. It is a proper way to keep the מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: וְכָךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן,
phrases.english: And this was the practice of Rabbi Tarfon,
that he would take (the redemption money) and return it.
phrases.notes: רבי טרפון was a כהן, so fathers brought him the five סלעים.

phrases.english: And when the Sages heard of the matter,
they said: This one has fulfilled this halakha.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 10 with a real case that shows the rule in action.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן may take the redemption money and give it back as a gift. רבי טרפון did this, and the חכמים praised it.

steps.title: Only this one הלכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the wording: did רבי טרפון keep only this one הלכה and nothing else?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This הלכה' and nothing more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the words 'this man kept this הלכה'. Read plainly, they sound like רבי טרפון kept only this one rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון was a giant who kept many הלכות. So the praise cannot mean that this was the only one. The wording needs fixing.

phrases.english: This halakha and nothing more?
phrases.notes: The גמרא isn't really doubting רבי טרפון here; it's poking at the wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the praise in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'קיים זה הלכה זו' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read literally, it sounds like רבי טרפון kept just this one הלכה. That cannot be true of such a great sage.

steps.title: He kept even this הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: the חכמים meant that רבי טרפון kept even this הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as: 'This man kept even this הלכה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by adding one word, 'אף' (even). Now the praise reads the right way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that רבי טרפון was so careful that he kept even this small, easy-to-miss detail: taking the money and returning it. The praise means 'this too', not 'only this'.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, קִיֵּים זֶה אַף הֲלָכָה זוֹ.
phrases.english: Rather, this one fulfilled even this halakha.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, קִיֵּים זֶה אַף הֲלָכָה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The praise sounded like רבי טרפון kept only this one הלכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The praise means he kept even this הלכה, on top of all the others.

steps.title: רבי חנינא and the father who hinted for his money back
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא also used to take and return the money. Once a father kept walking back and forth in front of him, hinting that he wanted it back. רבי חנינא told him that he had never really decided to give the money, so his son was not redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא used to take the money and give it back. He saw a certain man walking back and forth in front of him. He said to him: 'You did not make up your mind to really give it. That is a bad thing, so your son is not redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets a limit on the 'take and return' practice. Returning the money only works if the father first gave it for real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's pacing showed that he gave the money expecting to get it back. So he never truly handed it over. Without a real, complete gift to the כהן, the פדיון does not work, even if the כהן later gives the money back.

keyTerms.meaning: takes and returns (Aramaic for נוטל ומחזיר)
going and coming, pacing back and forth

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן may give the money back as a gift. But the father must first give it fully, with no expectation of getting it back. If he gives it only 'on condition' in his heart, the son is not redeemed.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי חנינא was not against taking and returning; he did it himself! The problem was only this father's attitude. He never really meant to give the money.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a real practical limit for פדיון הבן. The father's giving must be a true, complete transfer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina was accustomed to take (the money) and return it.
phrases.notes: Some versions have ושקיל, in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is דשקיל.

phrases.english: He saw a certain man
who was walking back and forth in front of him,
phrases.notes: A hint that he wanted his money returned.

phrases.english: he said to him: You did not give with a full decision,
this is a bad thing,
therefore his son is not redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא הֲוָה רְגִיל דְּשָׁקֵיל וּמַהְדַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about taking and returning. This one shows when the practice fails.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the father gave the money expecting to get it back, the gift was not complete, and his son is not redeemed.

steps.title: Lost redemption money: where do we learn the father must still pay?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if a father set aside money for his son's פדיון and it got lost, he is still responsible. Then it asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who sets aside money for his son's redemption and it gets lost is responsible for it.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for its source. This step sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting the money aside does not make it the כהן's yet. So if it is lost, the father has not finished his duty and must pay again. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know it?

phrases.english: One who sets aside the redemption of his son, and it was lost,
is responsible for it.
From where do we derive this?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפְרִישׁ פִּדְיוֹן בְּנוֹ וְאָבַד חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתוֹ. מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the take-and-return topic and opens a new line of the משנה about lost money.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the father's responsibility when money he set aside for פדיון הבן is lost.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: learned from ערכין through the word 'ערך'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns it through a גזירה שוה. The word 'ערך' appears both by פדיון הבן and by ערכין, and with ערכין a person is responsible until he pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: We learn it from the word 'ערך' (valuation), which appears in both places, from the laws of ערכין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to 'מנלן'. A shared word links פדיון הבן to ערכין, where a person who pledged a valuation must pay no matter what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By פדיון הבן the פסוק says 'בערכך', and by ערכין it also says 'ערכך'. In ערכין, the person owes the money as a debt. If what he set aside is lost, he still owes it. The same word carries that rule over to פדיון הבן.

keyTerms.meaning: valuation, the word linking the two topics
the laws of pledging a person's 'value' to the Temple

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
It is derived from 'valuation' 'valuation', from the passage of valuations.
phrases.notes: A גזירה שוה: במדבר 18:16 says 'בערכך' and ויקרא 27:23 says 'ערכך'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'ערך' from ערכין, where the one who pledges is responsible until he pays.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: learned from the עולת ראייה through the word 'ריקם'
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי, in the name of רבי יונתן, gives a second source. The word 'ריקם' (empty) appears by פדיון הבן and by עולת ראייה. Just as a person is responsible for his עולת ראייה, he is responsible for the פדיון money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי said in the name of רבי יונתן: The פסוק says, 'Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem, and none shall appear before Me empty.' We learn 'empty' from 'empty' in the case of the עולת ראייה. Just as one is responsible for the עולת ראייה, so too one is responsible for פדיון הבן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second, different answer to the same question 'מנלן'. It uses a different shared word, 'ריקם', and links פדיון הבן to the offering a pilgrim brings on the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק that commands פדיון הבן also says 'ולא יראו פני ריקם'. That phrase also appears about the עולת ראייה. A person who set aside an עולת ראייה that got lost must bring another one. Through the word 'ריקם', the same rule applies to the five סלעים.

keyTerms.meaning: empty-handed, the word linking the two topics
the burnt offering brought when appearing at the בית המקדש on a רגל

steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, two sources are offered for why a father who loses the money he set aside must pay again: ריש לקיש learns it from 'ערך' (ערכין), and רבי יונתן learns it from 'ריקם' (עולת ראייה). The next steps show that רב פפא rejects using them for this rule and moves both teachings to the clause about a son who died after thirty days.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi says in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:
'And every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem,'
'and none shall appear before Me empty' (Exodus 34:20),
and he derives 'empty' 'empty' from the burnt offering of appearance,
phrases.notes: שמות 23:15 uses 'ריקם' about appearing on the רגלים.

phrases.english: just as with the burnt offering of appearance one is responsible for it,
so too with the redemption of the son one is responsible for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different source for the same rule that ריש לקיש explained in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'ריקם' from עולת ראייה, which one must replace if it is lost.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: This is a proposed second source for the lost-money rule. רב פפא rejects it for this rule (Steps 18-19), and the גמרא moves it to the first clause, where it teaches that heirs must pay (Step 23).

steps.title: רב פפא: Why bring a verse when the משנה already has one?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא attacks the previous answers. The משנה already gives its own verse, so there is no need to bring another verse to prove the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא challenges this: Do we need a verse to support a verse?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on the sources brought by ריש לקיש and רב דימי for the rule that a father is responsible for lost פדיון money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה itself already quotes a verse as the reason for this rule. Bringing a גזירה שוה to prove what a verse already proves is unnecessary. So the previous answers seem to be in the wrong place.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges it (a strong objection to what was just said)
A verse for a verse (why bring a second verse to prove what a verse already proves?)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa challenges it:
A verse for a verse?
phrases.notes: The משנה already cites a verse, so why do we need another one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the two source answers given in steps 16 and 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The sources from ריש לקיש and רב דימי for the father's responsibility for lost money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These sources are not needed, because the משנה already supplies its own verse for this rule.

steps.title: The source is the משנה's own verse
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the reason for the father's responsibility is the verse the משנה quotes: "יהיה לך... אך פדה תפדה".
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא says: This rule follows the reason the משנה itself teaches: "It shall be yours... but you shall surely redeem."
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the correct source for the rule about lost money: the verse the משנה already quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse the משנה quotes, "יהיה לך... אך פדה תפדה", says the בכור 'shall be yours' (the כהן's) but must be redeemed. So the father's duty is like a debt owed to the כהן until the money actually reaches him, and setting money aside does not end it. That is why no outside גזירה שוה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: As the reason it teaches (the משנה's own stated reason)
You shall surely redeem (the double wording implies an obligation that lasts until payment)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa says:
This follows the reason that it teaches:
"It shall be yours... yet you shall surely redeem."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected sources with the משנה's own verse
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father's responsibility for lost money comes from "אך פדה תפדה", the verse already quoted in the משנה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's teaching belongs on the first clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that ריש לקיש's statement was really said about the first clause of the משנה, not about lost money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when the statement of ריש לקיש was said, it was said about the first clause.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא moves ריש לקיש's teaching to a different part of the משנה, and the next steps will quote that part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא does not throw away ריש לקיש's גזירה שוה. He only moves it to a case where the משנה gives no verse, so the derivation is now needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And when it was stated (introduces where a statement really belongs)

phrases.english: And when the statement of Reish Lakish was said,
it was said on the first clause:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אִיתְּמַר דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אַרֵישָׁא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Saves ריש לקיש's teaching by giving it a new location
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocation of a statement to a different clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש was explaining why a father must pay when the money set aside was lost
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש was explaining the earlier clause about a son who died after thirty days

steps.title: Son died after thirty days: what is the source that the father still pays?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first clause: if the son died after thirty days and the father had not paid, he must still pay. Then it asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he died after thirty days, even though he did not give, he must give. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the earlier clause of the משנה and asks for its source. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once thirty days pass, the obligation to pay five סלעים begins. The question is why the obligation stays even though the son, the one being redeemed, is no longer alive.

keyTerms.meaning: He died after thirty days (after the obligation began)
He must give (the five סלעים to the כהן)
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: If he died after thirty days,
even though he did not give,
he must give.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the clause that ריש לקיש's teaching is now attached to
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a father must pay פדיון money even after the son died, once thirty days have passed
steps.confusionAlert: This is a different case from step 15. There the money was lost. Here the son died. ריש לקיש's גזירה שוה is now being used for the son who died.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Learned from ערכין
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns it from a גזירה שוה of the word "ערך" in פדיון הבן and in ערכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: We learn "ערך" from "ערך" in ערכין.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the source for the case of the son who died: a גזירה שוה from ערכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ערכין, if someone pledged a person's value and that person died, he must still pay. The same applies to פדיון הבן: once the obligation began after thirty days, the son's death does not cancel it. The גמרא is repeating ריש לקיש's words, but now for a new purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes (it is learned through a link between verses)
Valuation (the word found in both passages)
Pledges of a person's set value to the Temple

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
It is derived from "valuation" and "valuation" in the passage on valuations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָתְיָא עֵרֶךְ עֵרֶךְ מֵעֲרָכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from ערכין: just as a pledge of value is still owed after the person dies, the פדיון is still owed after the son dies.

steps.title: רב דימי: Heirs are obligated, like with עולת ראייה
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי in the name of רבי יונתן links פדיון הבן to עולת ראייה through the word "ריקם". Just as heirs must bring the offering, heirs must pay the פדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי said in the name of רבי יונתן: "And all the firstborn of your sons you shall redeem, and none shall appear before Me empty." Just as there the heirs are obligated, so too here the heirs are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי's teaching is also moved. It now teaches that if the father died after the obligation began, his heirs must pay the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse puts פדיון הבן right next to "ולא יראו פני ריקם", which is about the עולת ראייה. With an עולת ראייה, if a man died after becoming obligated, his heirs must bring it. So once the obligation for פדיון הבן takes effect, it passes on to the heirs too.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there (in the source case)

phrases.english: Rav Dimi says in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:
"And all the firstborn of your sons you shall redeem,
and none shall appear before Me empty,"
just as there the heirs are obligated,
phrases.notes: With the עולת ראייה, heirs must bring the offering their father owed.

phrases.english: so too here the heirs are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second derivation for the first clause, which adds that the obligation passes to heirs
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Through "ריקם": just as heirs must bring an עולת ראייה that was owed, heirs must pay a פדיון that was owed.
steps.whatToRemember: After רב פפא: the lost-money rule comes from "פדה תפדה" in the משנה. ריש לקיש (ערכין) and רב דימי (עולת ראייה, heirs) explain why the obligation stays after the son or father dies once thirty days have passed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An obligation of פדיון הבן that has taken effect is a lasting debt. Death does not cancel it, and heirs must pay it.

steps.title: New משנה: The firstborn's double share and its limits
steps.stepSummary: The בכור takes a double share of his father's property, but not of his mother's property, not of growth in value after the death, and not of property only due to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The בכור takes a double portion of the father's property. He does not take a double portion of the mother's property. He does not take it from the increase in value, and not from what was due as he does from what was possessed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, moving from פדיון הבן to the בכור's double inheritance and its limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double share is real but limited. It applies only to the father's property and only to what the father actually held at his death. It does not apply to growth after his death or to property that was only coming to him (ראוי).

keyTerms.meaning: Increase in value after the father's death
Property due to come to the father but not yet in his hands

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: הַבְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּנִכְסֵי הָאָב,
phrases.english: The firstborn takes a double portion of the father's property,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּנִכְסֵי הָאֵם,
phrases.english: but does not take a double portion of the mother's property,
and he does not take it from the enhancement,
nor from property due as from property possessed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּנִכְסֵי הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the inheritance of the בכור
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בכור's double share applies only to the father's property that the father actually held at death. It does not apply to the mother's property, to later growth in value, or to property that was only due to him.
steps.confusionAlert: "Not בראוי" does not mean the בכור loses his status or his regular share. He still inherits these assets like any son. He just does not get the extra double portion from them.
